title: introduce-cost-scenario-synthesizer-cli-and-service
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: teams need a fast way to reason about unit economics across batching, prefill/caching, and quantization settings without running expensive cluster-wide experiments. This PR introduces a small service and a developer CLI that synthesize cost/latency projections from a configurable workload profile and a library of batching/cache/quant defaults. The feature provides: 1) rw-cost-sim CLI to run offline scenarios and export CSV/JSON reports; 2) a lightweight cost simulation endpoint (internal API /api/v1/cost/simulate) used by the Console and automation; 3) a catalog of tenant and SKU-level default profiles (batch sizes, prefills, quant tiers) and a deterministic composition engine to combine them; 4) a telemetry reconciliation step that can take a sample of real traces and seed the simulator to produce conservative estimates. The description below summarizes changes, design choices, and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1429) - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Telemetry mapping validated for major metrics - [x] Docs and Console wiring included - [x] No breaking API changes to public inference endpoints High-level goals: provide a fast, reproducible local/CI-friendly simulator for cost impact analysis; make it easy for Platform/Customer Success to propose safe defaults; surface warnings when a suggested quant/batch combo may violate latency SLOs. Migration/compatibility: defaults are additive and behind a runtime flag; existing tenant configs are unchanged until auto-apply is explicitly enabled by the operator. Performance: the simulator runs deterministically in ~3-12s per scenario on CI sample hardware; service endpoint is rate-limited behind auth and intended for internal tooling only. Rollout: staged behind feature-flag, Console beta, then automatic suggestions for eligible tenants.

design_notes: Simulator model: consumer-facing scenario DSL captures arrival rate, size distribution, temperature of requests, and optional sample traces. The synthesizer composes: 1) batch pipeline (microbatching shapes + continuous batch curve), 2) prefill/cache model (hit rates, TTLs, prefix reuse), 3) quant tier performance model (per-token throughput multipliers and quality/latency tradeoffs). We ship conservative defaults for tenant classes (startup/midmarket/enterprise) and allow operators to attach tenant-specific overrides. Telemetry reconciliation maps observed per-request token counts, prefix reuse, and tail latency to seed values; we bias estimates slightly higher to avoid optimistic guidance. The service is intentionally read-only; auto-apply feature will be a separate PR with careful rollout and operator opt-in.
tests: Unit tests cover profile composition and SLO checks. Integration tests run simulated scenarios against a local lightweight runtime to validate cost and latency projections. Added CI job cost-sim-integration which runs a minimal set of scenarios under 3 tuning knobs (batch, cache, quant). E2E smoke exercised Console wiring and export endpoint.

Console page includes an export button and an inline explanation of conservative assumptions.
release_notes: Added Cost Scenario Synthesizer (rw-cost-sim) and internal cost simulation API: allows teams to model batching, caching, and quantization impacts on unit economics. Non-breaking; behind feature flag. Includes Console beta integration and exportable reports.
manual_rollout_steps: 1) Enable feature-flag for internal customers, 2) run sample scenarios for a few tenants and compare to telemetry, 3) open Console beta to Platform, 4) collect feedback and adjust default profiles, 5) roll out to broader tenants if conservative estimates align.
notes_for_support: If customers see large deltas vs observed billing, collect a sample trace bundle (see docs) and run rw-cost-sim --reconcile to produce a reconciled projection. Default profiles are conservative and intended to avoid underestimation.
security_considerations: Service endpoint is internal-only and requires service token; CLI does not ship any credentials by default. Telemetry ingestion uses limited sample data; no PII expected. Audit logs added for simulation runs.
